name: meridian-mailroom
description: AI mail-triage pipeline for a disability law firm: classify, extract, fuzzy-match, route, with a human gate. Live demo, synthetic data.

paragraphs: An AI mail-triage pipeline for a disability law firm, shown as a working internal tool. Incoming scanned mail is classified, has its identifiers extracted, is fuzzy-matched to the right client, and is routed automatically, except for high-stakes letters, which are held for a human before anything happens to them.
Live demo: Everything here is synthetic. Fictional firm, fictional agency, invented people, no real client data.

Law firms drown in mail. A disability practice gets denials, award notices, hearing notices, exam appointments, records requests, and overpayment letters, hundreds a week, each of which has to be read, filed under the right client and matter, and acted on before a deadline slips. This is the pattern I build for that problem, reduced to its architecture and rebuilt on synthetic data so it can be shown in public.
features: A human-review gate that fires before any action. Denials, awards, appeal
Fuzzy matching that survives OCR. Scanned mail is full of typos. "R0bert Castiilo"
An append-only audit log. Every run and every review decision writes one immutable
